name: Vansen AugMount Installation Technician Full Rig
description: Charcoal heavy-canvas work jacket with aug-channel seams at both shoulders and forearms, worn over insulated gray work trousers with reinforced knee patches and cable-management loops at the hip. A magnification visor with dual articulating lenses flips down from a padded head harness, and an integrated ear-cup blocks high-decibel servo noise. Heavy-duty insulated gloves with conductive fingertip pads allow precision torque and live-current testing. Steel-capped composite boots with anti-static soles ground against discharge, and a double-wrap tool roll at the waist holds drivers, calibration keys, and a nerve-signal tester.
functionality: Conductive fingertip gloves allow live-current testing during aug installation without removing hand protection; anti-static boot soles prevent discharge near sensitive neural interfaces.
what_it_says: This person bolts the future onto other people's bodies for a living, and they're precise enough to do it without killing anyone.
story_hooks: The nerve-signal tester in the tool roll has a hidden secondary mode that can read — and transmit — a freshly installed aug's calibration data.
One of the calibration keys on the tool roll opens a neural lock that hasn't been manufactured in seven years.
